title: Paid Idioms PART - (II) SSC CGL PRE 2024

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
All his friends admired him because he was a straight shooter
questions.solution: A) A straight shooter(idiom) – A thoroughly upright straightforward person (ईमानदार और स्पष्टवादी व्यक्ति)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
My uncle lives in New York, so I only see him once in a blue moon.
questions.solution: D)Once in a blue moon(idiom) – Something that happens rarely or not very often. कभी-कभार होना।

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Radhika stood by Monica’s side through thick and thin.
options: 1) Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica’s safety and security
2) In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time
3) In the moments when Monica couldn’t complete some simple tasks
4) Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult
questions.solution: D)Through thick and thin(idiom) – Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult किसी भी स्थिति में, चाहे परिस्थिति कितनी भी कठिन या चुनौतीपूर्ण क्यों न हो डटे रहना है

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
In my new office, all employees were different, so I felt like a fish out of water.
questions.solution: D)Fish out of water(idiom) – Uncomfortable असहजता

questions.question:
Read the sentence carefully and select the most suitable idiom to fill in the blank.
The renowned publisher decided to withdraw a book from the market. No one was interested in the book as the arguments presented were ____________.
questions.solution:
C)Beside the mark(idiom) – not relevant to the topic; not accurate or appropriate. विषय से बाहर
Under the rose(idiom) – in secret; privately. गुप्त रूप से
High and mighty(idiom) – behaving in a superior or arrogant manner. घमंडी
Out of the woods(idiom) – out of danger or difficulty. खतरे से बाहर

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
My sisters wished me good luck before I went on the stage to sing.
options: 1) Told me to break an arm
2) Told me to break the ice
3) Told me to sit on the fence
4) Told me to break a leg
questions.solution:
D)Told me to break a leg(idiom) – A way of wishing someone good luck, especially before a performance प्रदर्शन से पहले शुभकामनाएं देने का एक तरीका
Told me to break an arm– Incorrect phrase, doesn't convey the same meaning
Told me to break the ice(idiom) – To initiate conversation or create a relaxed atmosphere बातचीत की शुरुआत करना या माहौल को सहज बनाना
Told me to sit on the fence(idiom) – To remain neutral and not take sides निष्पक्ष रहना और किसी पक्ष में न होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Anand personally believes in the motto, “When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.”
options: 1) Earn the maximum out of business
3) Enjoy the most when the season is favourable
4) Make the best out of difficult situation
questions.solution: D)When life gives you lemons, make lemonade(idiom) – Make the best out of a difficult situation कठिन परिस्थिति से सर्वश्रेष्ठ निकालना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
In those days, we did not expect luxuries; we were thankful if we could keep the wolf from the door.
questions.solution: C)Keep the wolf from the door(idiom) – Avoid starvation दरिद्रता से बचना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
My cousin works day and night to achieve success in life.
questions.solution: A)Around the clock– Working continuously without stopping (idiom) – निरंतर काम करना.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.
To bring to light
questions.solution: A)To bring to light(idiom) – To disclose (प्रकट करना(

questions.question:
Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Rina pulled a long face since her husband had not bought her a diamond necklace on their anniversary.
questions.solution: B) Pulled a long face (idiom)– To look saddened उदास दिखना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Cut corners
options: 4) Do something in an inexpensive and easy way
questions.solution: D)Cut corners(idiom) –Do something in an inexpensive and easy wayसस्ता और आसान तरीका अपनाना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Easy does it
options: 1) Used to tell someone to do something rarely
2) Used to tell someone to do something violently
3) Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully
4) Used to tell someone to do something horridly
questions.solution: C)Easy does it(idiom) – Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully. धीरे-धीरे और सावधानी से कुछ करने के लिए कहा जाता है।

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill the blank in the given situation.
I thought Sadhna would always stick by me, but when I got into trouble, she turned out to be a/an ___________.
questions.solution:
B)Fair-weather friend(noun) – A person who stops being a friend in times of difficulty. मुसीबत के समय साथ छोड़ने वाला दोस्त
Hard nut to crack(idiom) – A difficult problem or situation to deal with. कठिन समस्या
White elephant(idiom) – A possession that is useless or troublesome, especially one that is expensive to maintain. बेकार और महंगा सामान
Open secret(noun) – Something that is supposed to be secret but is actually widely known. ऐसा राज जो सबको पता हो

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the idiom in the given brackets.
His PhD degree seems to be (Penelope’s web).
questions.solution: B)Penelope’s web(idiom) –An endless task(अंतहीन कार्य)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given group of words.
On cloud nine
questions.solution: D)On cloud nine(idiom) – Being very delighted (बहुत खुश होना)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given group of words.
A bitter pill
questions.solution:
C) Facing a distressing situation
A bitter pill(idiom) –A situation that is unpleasant but must be accepted कड़वी सच्चाई

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Creature of habit
options: 4) One who does same thing in the same way
questions.solution: D)Creature of habit(idiom) – One who does the same thing in the same way, आदतों का दास

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hit the roof
questions.solution: C)Hit the roof(idiom) – To become very angry (बहुत गुस्सा होना)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Let the dust settle
options: 1) Wait for the other person to make a move
2) To wait for a situation to become clear or certain
4) To make use of a situation
questions.solution: B)Let the dust settle(idiom) – To wait for a situation to become clear or certain. किसी स्थिति के स्पष्ट या निश्चित होने का इंतजार करना।
